WASHINGTON , Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Vanda Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Vanda) (Nasdaq: VNDA ) today announced financial and operational results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.
"We are pleased with the strong revenue growth in the third quarter, increasing 24% year-over-year, driven by continued Fanapt momentum and the early contribution from our NEREUS commercial launch, while operating expenses decreased 18% compared to the second quarter as key Phase III and launch-preparation activities conclude," said Mihael H. Polymeropoulos, M.D., Vanda's President, CEO and Chairman of the Board. "Looking ahead, with the commercial launch of BYSANTI expected in the fourth quarter, the Quimilza BLA under FDA review with a December PDUFA date, and positive Phase III results supporting potential expansions for NEREUS in GLP-1 -induced vomiting and HETLIOZ in Delayed Sleep-Wake Phase Disorder, we are focused on further moderating costs and driving revenue growth from our current portfolio and planned launches to support sustainable long-term value."
During 2025 and 2026, Vanda has advanced multiple Phase III programs, continued its commercial activities for Fanapt Â® (iloperidone), HETLIOZ Â® (tasimelteon) and PONVORY Â® (ponesimod) and prepared for the commercial launches, including manufacturing commercial supplies, of NEREUSâ¢ (tradipitant), BYSANTIâ¢ (milsaperidone), and Quimilzaâ¢ (imsidolimab). These activities resulted in significantly increased operating expenses in 2025 and 2026. As certain of these activities began concluding in Q3 2026, operating expenses have decreased and Vanda expects operating expenses to decrease further in future quarters, as the remainder of these activities conclude.
Total net product sales were $69.8 million in Q3 2026, a 24% increase compared to $56.3 million in Q3 2025 and a 38% increase compared to $50.5 million in Q2 2026. Total net product sales includes approximately $7.0 million of HETLIOZ Â® revenue for orders shipped on June 29, 2026 that arrived on July 1, 2026.
Total operating expenses were $93.3 million in Q3 2026, a 7% increase compared to $87.5 million in Q3 2025 and an 18% decrease compared to $114.3 million in Q2 2026.

These orders were recognized as revenue in Q3 2026.

Since commercial expansion following the approval of bipolar disorder, Fanapt Â® has seen significant growth, with TRx 1 up 72% and NBRx 1 up 306% versus Q2 2024.

BYSANTIâ¢ is protected by data exclusivity through February 20, 2031 and multiple patents, the latest of which expires on May 31, 2044.

Key Regulatory & Clinical Development Highlights
In October 2026, Vanda announced positive results from the Phase III clinical study, VP-VLY-686-3601, of NEREUSâ¢ for the prevention of vomiting associated with GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy. Vanda intends to discuss the results with the FDA and plans to submit a supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) seeking approval of NEREUSâ¢ for the prevention of vomiting associated with GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy.
In September 2026, Vanda announced positive topline results from the pivotal Phase III study of HETLIOZ Â® in adults with Delayed Sleep-Wake Phase Disorder (DSWPD). Vanda intends to discuss these data with the FDA and to submit an sNDA seeking approval of HETLIOZ Â® for DSWPD. If approved, HETLIOZ Â® would be the first FDA-approved medicine indicated for this condition.
The Biologics License Application (BLA) for Quimilzaâ¢ in Generalized Pustular Psoriasis (GPP) is under review by the FDA with a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of December 12, 2026. The results of the pivotal clinical study were published in the April 28, 2026 issue of the New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM) Evidence 2 .
The Phase III study of BYSANTIâ¢ as a once-daily adjunctive treatment for major depressive disorder (MDD) is ongoing, with results expected in the first half of 2027. The study is enrolling patients in 54 sites in the U.S. and Europe and has enrolled 55% of the 500 patient enrollment target. The primary endpoint of the study is the change from baseline to week 6 of the Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) comparing milsaperidone and placebo. Secondary endpoints include Clinical Global Impression â Severity (CGI-S) and Clinical Global Impression â Change (CGI-C).
Vanda continues to progress the FDA formal hearing regarding HETLIOZ Â® for the treatment of jet lag disorder. The proceeding, a rare administrative hearing process granted after the D.C. Circuit set aside the FDA's prior refusal to approve the application, is advancing according to schedule and is expected to culminate in a five-day hearing before the Administrative Law Judge from December 14, 2026 to December 18, 2026.
Vanda continues to pursue its legal challenge to FDA's final order refusing to hold a hearing or to approve the Company's sNDA for HETLIOZ Â® in the treatment of insomnia. Following oral argument before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit in September 2026, the matter is awaiting decision.
Vanda continues to pursue its legal challenge to FDA's final order refusing to hold a hearing or to approve the Company's NDA for NEREUSâ¢ in gastroparesis. Briefing is currently underway before the DC Circuit, and is due to be completed in mid-November.
Net loss was $22.6 million (diluted loss per share of $0.37) in Q3 2026 compared with a net loss of $22.6 million (diluted loss per share of $0.38) in Q3 2025 and a net loss of $62.5 million (diluted net loss per share of $1.04) in Q2 2026.
Net loss was $133.6 million (diluted loss per share of $2.23) in the first nine months of 2026 compared with a net loss of $79.3 million (diluted loss per share of $1.35) in the first nine months of 2025.
Vanda is updating its 2026 financial guidance and expects to achieve total revenue for full year 2026 of greater than $240 million.
